## Plan

I looked at three files in both versions and confirmed the difference.

**Files that differ**
- `/workspace/src/click/core.py` vs the reference copy — the function that decides the help option names (`get_help_option_names`, around line 1177).
- `/workspace/tests/test_commands.py` vs the reference copy — the reference adds several new checks for that function.
- `/workspace/CHANGES.md` vs the reference copy — the reference adds one line to the 8.5.0 list.

**What the current code does (verified by reading `/workspace/src/click/core.py`)**
- The function at line 1177 collects the help option names into a plain collection that does not keep order: it starts from `set(ctx.help_option_names)` (line 1179), then removes any name that another parameter already uses via `difference_update` on `param.opts` and `param.secondary_opts` (lines 1181-1182), and returns the result.
- Because it uses a set, the order in which the names were given is lost. So if a user writes the help names as `["-h", "--help"]`, the names come back in some other, unpredictable order.
- `Context.help_option_names` defaults to `["--help"]` and can be inherited from a parent context (lines 452-459), so this matters whenever someone sets more than one name.

**What the reference does**
- It keeps the names in the exact order they were declared, removes repeated names while keeping the first one seen, and still drops any name already used by another parameter (including feature-switch style names).
- The result is a stable, predictable order instead of a shuffled one.

**What is missing / wrong for the user today**
- There is no way to make the help option keep the order the user asked for. The order can change between runs.
- There are no checks in the current `/workspace/tests/test_commands.py` that pin the order of help option names.

**Files in the WORKSPACE about the problem (these go in Hints)**
- `/workspace/src/click/core.py`
- `/workspace/tests/test_commands.py`
- `/workspace/CHANGES.md`

I could not read any further files (tool budget), so I will only make claims about these three paths.

**Draft ticket outline (plain, user voice)**
- Title: Help option names come back in a mixed-up order.
- What happens now: when more than one help name is given, the list that comes back is not in the order given.
- What should happen: the names should stay in the order given, repeats removed, and names taken by other options still left out.
- About this project: Click is a tool for people building command-line programs; it builds the options and help text.
- Problem this solves: people who choose their own help names get them in the wrong order, so the help output is confusing.
- What changed: names keep their declared order, duplicates are dropped, and names used by other options are still removed.
- Impact: usability and correctness.
- User experience: before, two names might show up swapped; after, they show up exactly as written.
- Hints: the three paths above.

{"file_path": "/megabit/ticket.md", "content": "# My help option names come back in a mixed-up order

## What happens now
When I give my command more than one name for the help option, the names come back in
a mixed-up order instead of the order I wrote them. If I write the names as short one
first and long one second, the program may show them the other way around. The order
can be different from what I asked for, so I cannot rely on it.

## What should happen
The help option names should stay in the same order I wrote them. If I write the same
name twice, only the first one should be kept. Names that another option already uses
should still be left out. I should be able to set the names and then see them exactly
as I arranged them.

## About this project
This project is a tool for people who build command-line programs in Python. It takes
care of reading the options a user types, printing the help text, and showing errors.
People use it so they do not have to write all of that themselves.

## Problem this solves
People who pick their own short and long names for the help option get them back in a
random order, so the help text can look wrong and confuse the people using their
program. This matters most when a name they chose clashes with another option and the
leftover names come out shuffled.

## What changed
The help option names now keep the order in which they were given. Names that appear
more than once are trimmed so the first one stays. Names that another option already
uses are still removed. Before, the order was lost; now it is kept.

## Impact
Ease of use and correctness.

## User experience
Before: I set the help names as the short one first and the long one second, and the
program sometimes shows them swapped. After: I set the same two names and they show up
exactly in that order every time.

## Hints
- /workspace/src/click/core.py
- /workspace/tests/test_commands.py
- /workspace/CHANGES.md"}
